speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This two-pronged approach has benefited consumers and businesses which seek to serve their customers well, and helped resolve disagreements between businesses and consumers amicably.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: It is important for consumers to know their rights and be alert to unfair trading practices so that they can be in a good position to make sound purchasing decisions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: To this end, the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) works closely with the Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE) which plays a key role in championing consumer education and raising consumer awareness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: CASE also helps consumers to resolve disputes with businesses through negotiation and mediation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The majority of consumer disputes with businesses are resolved, in fact, in this way.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act (CPFTA) is a key pillar in our consumer protection framework.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Act provides for civil actions to stop errant businesses which engage in unfair trading practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The errant businesses, where they do not comply with the VCAs and persist in unfair practices, in such cases, the CPFTA also empowers CASE and STB to apply for injunction action with the Courts to be brought against these businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Injunctions which are ordered by the Courts require errant businesses to cease the unfair practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For egregious cases that involve criminal activities, they are handled by the Police who will investigate and prosecute the errant businesses under the Penal Code and the Miscellaneous Offences (Public Order and Nuisance) Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Consumer education is a key pillar that underlines the entire framework.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: When consumers encounter a problem, our consumer protection framework provides for an escalating set of measures, ranging from negotiation and mediation, which is facilitated by CASE, to assist consumers in resolving disputes, or by taking up VCAs by retailers to stop unfair practices and compensate consumers, or civil actions through injunctions issued by the Courts for errant retailers, and if need be Police investigation and prosecution of egregious cases which involve criminal activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: So, it is a set of escalating measures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Page: 67 Consumer education is a key and fundamental component as it is important that every consumer makes his or her purchases with a clear evaluation of the many choices he or she is exposed to and understand the terms and obligations of the contracts he or she is entering into.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: As the old adage goes, "Knowledge is power".

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Consumers who are aware of their rights are better able to make sound purchasing decisions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The majority of businesses engage in fair trading and seek to serve their customers well, maintain a good business reputation and aim to advance their business interests through positive sharing via "word of mouth" and, in this modern era of the Internet, through social media as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: However, a small number of errant businesses have, unfortunately, continued to engage in unfair practices and take advantage of consumers, both locals and tourists.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This affects consumer confidence and dents our reputation as a shopping destination.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We saw this happen during the Mobile Air incident at the end of 2014.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: MTI carried out a review of the CPFTA in 2015 to study how our consumer protection framework can be further strengthened.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We are conscious of the need to take a balanced approach, as overly onerous measures can impose unnecessary business costs which would ultimately be passed on to customers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: So, along the whole spectrum, we identified a gap in the injunction process.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: It is slow, as CASE and STB have no investigation and enforcement powers and hence, faced operational difficulties in gathering evidence to submit their applications to the Courts to file an injunction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Some errant businesses have also sidestepped injunctions by closing their businesses and setting up new ones.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: As part of our review, we studied the best practices and experiences of other jurisdictions, such as Hong Kong and Australia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We also engaged stakeholders, including CASE, the Singapore Retailers Association, individual retailers, and the Sim Lim Square Management Committee.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: They are supportive of the proposed amendments, and provided views which we considered.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We also carried out a public consultation exercise over four weeks this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The respondents to the public consultation expressed support for the proposed amendments, including strengthening the injunction process, and some of their feedback have been incorporated in the proposed amendments and finalisation of this Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: SPRING Singapore is the best positioned Government agency to administer the CPFTA as its mandate is to oversee the growth of enterprises in Singapore, including aspects of consumer protection, such as standards and product safety.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Currently, the CPFTA does not provide CASE and STB with investigation and enforcement powers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Hence, they face challenges in gathering evidence to file injunction applications with the Courts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Under the new Part 3B of the same clause, any person who obstructs SPRING Singapore's investigations such as by destroying documents and providing SPRING Singapore with false Page: 68 information, will be committing an offence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: CASE and STB's previous roles as specified bodies under the CPFTA which can submit injunction applications will be repealed to avoid duplication of effort.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: CASE and STB, however, will remain the first points of contact for locals and tourists, and will focus on assisting consumers with their disputes, including obtaining redress or compensation through negotiation, mediation and VCAs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: CASE and STB will surface cases of errant retailers to SPRING Singapore for further investigation and action.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: With the appointment of SPRING Singapore as the administering agency, two consequential changes have become necessary.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: First, clause 14 amends the Standards, Productivity and Innovation Board Act to expand SPRING Singapore's functions and powers for the administration and enforcement of the CPFTA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Second, clauses 5 and 11 abolish the Injunction Proposals Review Panel (IPRP).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The IPRP's role was to ensure that CASE and STB only file applications for injunction for serious cases since these two agencies previously did not have investigation powers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: As SPRING Singapore is empowered to gather evidence to file injunction applications, it is no longer necessary to retain the IPRP.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These relate to additional measures which may be imposed by the Courts on errant businesses as part of the injunction orders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Courts may make injunction orders which restrain errant businesses from engaging in unfair practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Clauses 4 and 5 provide for the additional measures or accompanying orders that a Court may take or make in addition to an injunction order.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These accompanying orders serve to raise consumer awareness of errant businesses, both business entities and individuals, who are under injunction orders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: They also make it harder for errant businesses to sidestep injunction orders by closing businesses and setting up new ones under another person's name.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Taken together, the additional measures that the Courts may impose will enable SPRING Singapore to monitor these errant businesses and take swift enforcement action if the orders are not complied with.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For entities, clause 4 allows the Courts to require businesses to comply with additional measures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These can include notices to be put up at the shop fronts or on the landing pages of their websites.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Thirdly, all invoices issued by these entities may be required to incorporate the notice of the injunction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Page: 69 Fourth, the entities may be required to inform SPRING Singapore within 14 days of any changes to the business, such as number of premises, and the addresses at which the entities operate – new branches, for example.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This will enable SPRING Singapore to monitor them as part of the enforcement efforts and take timely action if they do not comply with the Curt orders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Fifth, entities may be required to reimburse SPRING Singapore for costs incurred to publish notices to raise consumer awareness of the commencement of injunction action or injunction order.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These are all aimed at raising consumers' awareness of a business under injunction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For individuals, be it employees or directors of the company for which an injunction order is served, clauses 4 and 5 provide for SPRING Singapore to take injunction action against these individuals, such as partners, and those who knowingly instigate and help errant businesses to engage in unfair practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This serves to dissuade individuals from helping errant businesses sidestep injunction orders by setting up new businesses and persisting with the unfair practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Courts may also require individuals who are under injunction orders to comply with additional measures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: First, the individuals may be required to publish notices of the injunction at their own cost.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Second, the individuals may be required to reimburse SPRING Singapore for costs incurred to publish notices to raise again consumer awareness of the commencement of injunction action or injunction order.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Third, they may be required to inform SPRING Singapore as well within 14 days of any changes to their employment which involves consumer transactions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We also took in CASE's suggestion to include changes to shareholdership of businesses that engage in consumer transactions as a notifiable event to SPRING Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These measures will enable SPRING Singapore to monitor these individuals as part of its enforcement efforts and take timely action if they do not comply with Court orders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Taken together, the requirements for errant retailers to publicise the injunction orders and notify consumers of the injunction order prior to entering into a transaction, as well as SPRING Singapore working with CASE to publish injunction orders, will serve to raise consumers' awareness of retailers who are under injunction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Consumers can then decide if they still want to purchase from the retailer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This goes back to the principle of "caveat emptor", buyers beware, with consumers exercising their choice and making informed purchasing decisions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Page: 70 Mdm Speaker, our approach to consumer protection is a balanced one.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In drafting this Bill, we have taken great care to ensure that it is both pro-consumer and business friendly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The legislation is just one part of the entire consumer protection framework.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Consumer education is the key plank in this whole process and MTI is working to operationalise the proposed amendments by the end of this year.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The CPFTA provides consumers with protection from unfair practices and offers consumers a simpler recourse to civil remedies against errant retailers who engage in unfair practices.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Under the Act, the Government empowers specified bodies like CASE and the STB to take action against suppliers who engage or are likely to engage in unfair practice.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: As Specified Bodies, CASE and STB are empowered to invite a supplier to sign a VCA and even to apply to Court for an injunction against errant trade suppliers.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: However, there are limitations to the operation of CPFTA when dealing with dishonest retailers.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: An example would be the few dishonest retail operators at Sim Lim Square who were ripping off consumers and tourists.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Their antics were reported in the media in late 2014.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Instead of selling their products in an honest and ethical manner, these retailers practised deception and cheated consumers and tourists, and this resulted in many cries of foul play by consumers.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The actions of a few bad hats have affected the reputation of the other honest retailers in Sim Lim Square.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: CASE had worked with the Management Corporation Strata Title of Sim Lim Square.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: We helped them to set up a consumer complaint terminal, put up consumer alert notices naming retailers with the most number of complaints.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: However, there is little effect as consumers continued to be deceived and lured into buying products due to the perceived lower prices.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Once a consumer has made payment for the product, the retailer imposes additional costs like "phone unlocking fees" or "in-house insurance" and illegally refuses to allow the consumer to collect their Page: 71 purchased products.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The presence of such recalcitrant retailers who flout the law and engage in unfair practices suggests that more muscle must be given to the authorities to take punitive action.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: CASE does not have any power under the existing CPFTA to take criminal prosecution against dishonest retailers.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The Police often classify disputes between consumers and retailers as civil disputes.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: They refer consumers who had lodged Police reports to CASE.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The Police expects CASE to advise the consumers and retailers to resolve their disputes and to mediate a settlement.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: However, dishonest retailers are no respecter of the law.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Due to the perceived lack of action, a small minority of retailers persist with their unfair practices and consumers suffer when they are taken advantage of.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Court injunctions are also of no effect on retailers who are not serious about their business.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Out of the six injunctions taken out by CASE, every one of them had ceased operations after the injunction.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Some retailers who have signed VCAs had used the names of their relatives to set up another company to operate a new business, and this defeats the intent of VCAs and Court injunctions as any restrictions imposed can easily be overcome.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Thus, I welcome the amendments to the CPFTA to give SPRING Singapore the power to investigate, require production of documents and enter premises to inspect and seize documents.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: These are wide powers needed when dealing with errant retailers, and once the evidence has been obtained, SPRING Singapore has the power to apply for injunctions against egregious errant retailers.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I also support the provisions for SPRING Singapore to seek Court orders that require suppliers to publicise the details of the declaration or injunction and notify the consumer about the Court orders.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This will ensure that such retailers cannot try to cover up their unethical conduct.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This means that an injunction order can be extended to third parties like employees and agents and can even extend to family members of the supplier as long as they knowingly help the supplier to carry out unfair practices.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This will ensure that the injunction order cannot be sidestepped by using other people's names to start a new business.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Much as I am happy with the amendments, the proposed changes to the CPFTA are not a magic bullet to solve all consumer disputes.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The reality is that consumers, too, must do their part to exercise caution when buying goods or services from suppliers.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I just want to assure the Minister of State that CASE will do its part to continue to educate consumers on their duties as well.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: There are a few concerns which I hope that the Minister of State can address.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: First, much of the frustration in respect of the Sim Lim Square fiasco arose because the conduct of the supplier was not just about "unfair practice".

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: He cheated consumers by asking them to pay for non-existent unlocking phone fees or he could ask the consumers to buy fake compulsory insurance.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In such instances, any Court injunction by SPRING Singapore would be of limited effect as well.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This would be a stronger deterrent to crooks, compared to a Court injunction.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: They face imprisonment if they continue to behave in such criminal manner.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: If SPRING Singapore does not initiate contempt action, surely, retailers will not bother with any injunction taken up against them.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Second, I notice that the proposed amendments make no attempt to discourage the taking of prepayment or deposits for future services.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: CASE has always been concerned at the losses suffered by consumers who had paid deposits or made prepayments to companies which subsequently became insolvent.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: We had received many complaints from consumers who had lost money when travel agencies cease operations or when wedding boutiques or other companies go into liquidation.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: It was reported that one member paid $1,700 for a 26-month package just nine days before the company closed.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: When company managements behave in such a dishonest manner and consumers get cheated, something must be done.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I urge the Government to take strong action against the directors and management of any company whose management knowingly continues to collect large sums of prepayment when they are fully aware that the company is insolvent and cannot continue its operations.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This will send a strong signal to the directors and management of a company that they must not act dishonestly or recklessly.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Third, may I ask the Minister of State whether the Government would consider issuing a "grey" list of contractual terms which the Government considers to be unfair?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: It would help consumers and businesses alike to understand which contractual terms may be considered unfair.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: An example of such an unfair term which may be included in a "grey list" would be terms that require all disputes with consumers to be referred to arbitration.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The use of the arbitration clause in contracts makes it near impossible for consumers to seek redress for small claims as this is because arbitration is simple too expensive when the claims are too small.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I hope that the Minister of State can clarify my concerns.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Before I end my speech, I wish to acknowledge my appreciation to MTI for carrying out public consultation for the proposed changes.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I also thank the Minister and the staff from MTI for their strong support and constant engagement with CASE to improve consumer protection.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It will only take a few bad hats to give Singapore a very bad name, and we cannot afford that as Singapore is a major retail centre of the world.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It sets out the requirements of a prior written notice, for example, giving two working days' notice of the intended entry indicating the subject matter and the purpose of the investigation, and also to be accompanied by a copy of the alleged offences.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Under this provision, an investigation officer may be empowered to inspect and search the premises, take photos or videos of the premises or persons in the premises, seize or detain goods, bring necessary equipment, require someone at the premises to produce documents, or to take away information stored in digital form.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Clause 12(j) of the Bill then provides the power to enter premises under a Court warrant in cases where there are reasonable grounds for suspecting that there are documents on the premises which have not been produced or may be required to be produced, or where officers attempted to enter under the conditions in clause 12(i), but failed to do so.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We should not be lowering the threshold for entering premises and carrying out searches or seizures for different kinds of offences.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Let the Courts be a point of control and oversight to decide whether any entry, search or seizure is actually necessary.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The presence of a notice, while admittedly is better than no notice at all, does not take away the fact that the powers to enter and take photos, seize or detain without a Court warrant are rather draconian.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Let us not take such searches too lightly.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Carry out searches by all means, if the Court sanctions it.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But do not make it easier for searches to be carried without a warrant from the Court.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I am concerned that if it is not administered effectively and consistently by the authority, the injunctions will be less effective and may fail in preventing the very acts that the present Bill is seeking to prevent.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It will be too late when the customer enters into the transaction and is subject to unfair practices.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Above all, consumers, local or otherwise, must be confident that when they go into any shop in Singapore, whether in Orchard Road or Sim Lim Square, or when they shop online, they can, without question, expect retailers to behave honourably and ethically and will not engage in unfair practices.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Page: 74 Madam, I am in support of the proposed amendments in Schedule 2 which included various forms of conduct as unfair practices, but I also wonder whether the current Act and the proposed amendment Bill may be sufficient to deal with businesses where customers sign onto a term subscription package, like gym, spa, hair or nail salon, or travel packages.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: On the other hand, I also recognise that the discounts that come with a fixed term package may be attractive to customers.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I myself signed up with California Fitness many years ago, shortly after they opened in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And as my hon colleague, Mr Lim Biow Chuan has pointed out, California Fitness was recently in the news for its sudden collapse, leaving many customers who have signed up for valuable packages in the lurch.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My wife and I have also signed up regularly for foot massage packages.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Under the scheme, some form of deposits or insurance may be required for participating businesses, but the scheme does not cover all businesses and is dependent on CASE working out the arrangements and accreditations with the relevant trade associations.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This may already be in place by a voluntary or more limited basis than I am thinking here.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But, Madam, we really should do more to prevent retailers from looking to bulk payments for packages as quick and easy solutions for business cash flow, and to give consumers peace of mind when they sign up for term subscription packages.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Such schemes can be driven by good business incentives.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Government may even wish to consider incentives, such as suitable tax reliefs.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We must continue to maintain our reputation as a major retail centre in the world.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And to do this, we must continue to improve our consumer protection laws in a fair and responsible manner.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Previously, CASE primarily depended on mediation between the two parties.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: CASE has limited powers to investigate and punish errant retailers or service providers.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In particular, I am very happy that the Bill also covers renovation contractors.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: During my Meet-the-People Sessions (MPS), I have received several complaints from my residents against renovation contractors who have collected substantial sums of money and either did not do what they promised or did such a poor job that the flat is in a worse condition than before the renovation.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Upon receiving complaints, these contractors would then be uncontactable.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Some residents who pursue their case against these contractors in the SCT would find that the company is only a $2-company with very little assets and the contractor could easily set up another $2-company under another trade name.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Hopefully, this will also have a deterrent effect against unfair trade practices.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mdm Speaker, I thank MTI for introducing this Bill.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In the past year, I have received many complaints against renovation contractors from my residents.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Most of these complaints are about contractors not keeping their promises, bad services and delaying the completion date.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Some contractors even become uncontactable after receiving the down payment.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The registered capital of some errant businesses is only $2.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is futile even if the resident brings them to Court and wins the suit.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These businessmen can simply register another company with a mere $2.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Besides the company name, it is best to make public their contact details on the Internet as well, so that consumers can stay away from these businesses.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In English): Mdm Speaker, in conclusion, I would like to wish SPRING Singapore every success in its new role, and I reaffirm my support for the Bill.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I believe this Bill has come in a timely fashion to ensure that consumers are better protected.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: During my MPS, I have residents who had sought my assistance on timeshares which they had bought.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Many victims of timeshare companies were bamboozled into purchasing a timeshare package without them taking a closer look at the fine print of the "Membership Agreement" before signing up.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This marks the beginning of the horror stories associated with purchasing timeshares.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: These timeshare agreements have no exit clause, much to the detriment of the consumers who are hardly savvy with legal or contract terms before signing the membership agreement.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The reality is that many clauses revolve around the liability of the member, with little on the obligation and liability of the timeshare companies.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Unfortunately, the amendment to protect consumers against timeshare companies came much later, after many had already been cheated.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Using the law, the timeshare companies would engage law firms to act against their customers to enforce these one-sided contracts.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In fact, I am also saddened that some law firms are willing to act on behalf of timeshare companies as their clients to squeeze the hard-earned money of many ordinary people.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The timeshare business must be making good money.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It is then not surprising to find many timeshare companies belonging to the same person.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: When complaints are lodged against a particular timeshare company, the owner would just set up another timeshare company to cheat other victims.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Hence, it is not surprising to find the same legal firm acting on behalf of all these timeshare companies.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: These companies can be ethically and morally wanting and they operate just above the line on legality.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Clearly, their intention is to get members or customers to sign up and enforce prejudiced membership contracts or subscribing to their services in order to receive "easy money", without making a business commitment to deliver on their service promises.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The common modus operandi by these timeshare businesses and some online retailers is to use the legal framework as a vehicle to short-change regular Singaporeans to pay them for services not rendered or rendered in a way that does not commensurate the value that is paid to them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Three and a half decades before the CPFTA was first enacted, the advocacy of consumer rights in Singapore had already taken root with the inception of CASE.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: The familiarity of local consumers with CASE is a testament to how closely it has been identified with advancing the cause of consumers against unfair business practices in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Despite its lack of investigative or enforcement powers, CASE has achieved much through its promotion of consumer education, and an appreciation of the inter-dependence between consumers and retailers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Much has been done in this area over the years, but the lack of a Government agency to spearhead enforcement has been a noticeable gap.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: This gap has become even more glaring in recent years, as high-profile cases have demonstrated how the infamy of certain errant retailers easily spreads beyond our shores, threatening the reputation for quality and trustworthiness that our retail sector has painstakingly achieved among visitors from overseas.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: The appointment of a Government agency to this role will provide a dedicated and prominent enforcement arm that has been lacking from our consumer protection framework to date.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Many of the most egregious examples of errant business practices were only resolved with the involvement of the Police.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Getting the Police involved in conflicts arising from consumer affairs is not ideal, despite the fact that such an approach is considered normal in many other countries.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, with advances in business technologies, it is becoming increasingly difficult to track those who are ready to push the boundaries of what is acceptable under the law.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Page: 78 Clearly, it is time that a specialist agency to spearhead consumer protection is called for.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Such an agency should be capable of deploying the technological tools to match the potential threats presented by new and increasingly sophisticated forms of errant business practices.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: However, we have to be cautious about adopting an overly heavy-handed approach.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: It would be ironic if consumer protection legislation ends up raising the costs of doing business.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: If the costs to sellers increase, it will also hurt the smaller businesses.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: On the other hand, a lack of protection will also end up hurting responsible sellers, with those in the tourism-related sectors potentially the hardest hit.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Given how far the ripples of any case can spread, it is clear that an agency with sufficient resources and scope of oversight to address any problems which arise is called for.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Errant retailers can impose a parasitic cost on others in their business community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: By encouraging the growth of a network of shady operators engaging in unacceptable practices, errant retailers obscure the view of their neighbouring businesses about positive business opportunities, gradually sapping the confidence of those around them about their ability to expand in a positive manner.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Fortunately, relative to the size of the economy, problems with errant retailers have been confined to only a very small group.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Unfortunately, reports about how certain practices have arisen to exploit loopholes have a certain repetitive ring to them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: In view of this, it is important that the agency tasked with enforcing consumer protection laws takes a proactive approach.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: It is an appropriate recognition of the challenges that come with the advanced development of our business landscape.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Although there is no conclusive evidence that either is true, the statistics published on the CASE website about the top 10 categories in which complaints are received cover virtually all the main areas of domestic economic activity that we know.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Understanding whether the frequency of complaints from consumers about errant business practices is related to cyclical business activity would help in the management and education of potential areas of conflict.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: First, at the moment, SPRING Singapore has been tasked with investigative and enforcement powers under this amendment Bill.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: For the same reasons that I believe that the involvement of the Police in consumer disputes is not the correct approach, I would urge the agency, when it takes on the appointment under this Bill, to explore how to promote efficient Page: 79 and sustainable approaches to enforcement, with a view to keeping costs as low as possible.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While Singapore strives to be a business-friendly hub for companies, we must also ensure that justice prevails in the marketplace, where no party is able to take advantage of another.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am sure many of us will recall the amount of public anger stirred up in 2014 by the high-profile cases of errant companies at Sim Lim Square.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Citizen vigilantes took over social media to reveal his identity.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A crowdfunding campaign was set up to compensate the victim, and money continued to pour in until it raised 12 times the targeted amount.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This was a display of collective public action in Singapore, an angry society stirred up by a clear case of a bully taking advantage of another person.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A year later, we saw BreadTalk's soya milk saga.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When a customer is made to pay more than he or she agreed to, or when a product is misrepresented, it is a form of injustice which hits the raw nerves of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, I would like to raise a few concerns.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I note that after the Lemon Laws were enacted in 2012, CASE had published accessible public awareness materials to educate consumers about their rights.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the same way, we need education for consumers to reap the full benefits of this proposed law.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, it would be useful to reiterate the acts listed in the Second Schedule, specifying what constitutes unfair practices.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We could also explain what an "injunction" means in layman's terms and to educate consumers to stay clear from deals which seem too good to be true.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If this is not feasible as a nationwide campaign, then I would recommend at least for the Government to pay special attention to hotspots where numerous complaints have been received.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In 2014, Vietnamese and Chinese media picked up on these scams targeting foreign nationals, tainting Singapore's image as a trustworthy, tourist-friendly shopping hub.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ultimately, we are strengthening legislation to strengthen trust in our society.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While I support this Bill, I hope this is not the end goal.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As I frequently mention in my speeches, legislation cannot be the end goal.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We cannot legislate everything, and we cannot depend solely on legislation and enforcement of legislation for the moral progress of our nation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We have been called a "fine city", and I am afraid there is some truth in this label.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When I speak to primary school kids and ask them why they should not litter, for example, almost every reply is that you cannot litter as you will get a fine or must "pay money if you get caught".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is a sign that we have become over-reliant on laws.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I wish the replies were that we should not litter because it might harm the environment, it might pollute the ecosystem, it might make it unpleasant for others, or we should not litter because someone else has to pick up the litter.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But where are we heading as a society if everything we do or do not do is because there is a fine or penalty attached to it?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It does seem like we are doing the right things for the wrong reasons.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Fundamentally, we should have laws, but we should not solely and consistently focus on the laws.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Morals and values in an ideal world should not be dictated by laws.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And these cannot be taught in the classroom nor written in textbooks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, we, as parents, need to teach by example.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We, as parents, need to instil the values in our children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Two quotes sum up what I just said.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The first, and I quote, "Children close their ears to advice but open their eyes to example"; and the second, "Children learn from what you are than what you teach".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ultimately, we cannot just depend on legislation or depend on schools to strengthen trust and reduce cheating.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This may sound like a fantastical utopia, and I, a foolish idealist.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I have personally encountered such a society.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In July 2012, I was in the Solomon Islands, and I shared my experience in a Facebook post more than four years ago.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I wrote: "The people here show a level of trust I seldom see.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We had dinner in a restaurant on the first night.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We didn't have enough cash, and their credit card machine was not working.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The owner said, "Never mind, pay me another time!" We went back the next night, and we still did not have enough local currency, and the credit card machine was still not working and the owner said, "Never mind, just eat first and pay me another time!" We were complete strangers, and he did not ask us for any ID, nothing." In the concluding paragraph of that Facebook post, I wrote, "I felt what it was like to live amongst people so genuine, so trusting that I had to pinch myself so many times to make sure I wasn't dreaming." In April this year, Minister Shanmugam spoke about how a 10-year-old child can take public transport alone in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The amendments aim to deter errant retail practices and to publicise the occurrence of such practices so that consumers are aware of which retailers have received injunctions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Not only is it the right thing to do for the sake of fairness, it also yields economic benefits.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Moreover, consumer protection, by reducing information asymmetry and imbalances and power between consumers and retailers, also enhances the efficient operation of markets.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Being pro-market does not mean being simply pro-business but striking the right balance between being pro-business and pro-consumer.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In our General Election 2015 manifesto, the Workers' Party called for the Government to be more proactive in seeking Court injunction orders against errant retailers and also provide more resources to the Government bodies tasked with this role.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, I do have a number of clarifying questions and suggestions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will CASE be sufficiently resourced to assist in all cases where consumers may need assistance to pursue their complaints?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The kind of assistance that can and will be provided and the sequence of steps that can be expected when one files or requests for assistance in pursuing a complaint should be made very clear to all consumers.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is seen on the websites of some of the Australian state consumer protection agencies, like the New South Wales Fair Trading, for example.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Page: 82 Second, Sir, an enhanced enforcement regime presupposes that there are clear guidelines to retailers about what is and is not considered unethical or errant conduct, and that measures are taken to educate retailers about their obligations.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Unfair practices are defined in the Second Schedule of the CPFTA.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, many retailers will not be aware of these provisions or how they are operationalised and practised.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, my question here is: how will retailers be educated about their responsibilities under the CPFTA, and which agency is tasked with this responsibility?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Third, and in a parallel fashion, consumer protection also depends on consumers being aware of their rights and taking action when they experience errant conduct.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Which agency will be responsible for educating consumers and how?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In this context, I suggest that SPRING Singapore or another agency consider requiring more operators to display consumer protection posters or signs to remind consumers about their rights in the shopping environment.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Fourth, beyond just obtaining injunctions against errant conduct, will SPRING Singapore or another organisation under MTI look into requiring merchants to implement broad-based pan-industry measures that are fairer to consumers?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, in Australia, the Consumer and Competition Commission requires grocery stores to display unit prices clearly for the produce that they sell.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: That Commission also defines certain types of contract clauses as oppressive and, hence, illegal.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will this kind of proactive preventive groundwork also be done in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I suggest that an agency, which could be SPRING Singapore, the Competition Commission of Singapore or another agency, be tasked to proactively require the whole industry to adopt fair consumer practices on an industry level in this way.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Fifth, SPRING Singapore is primarily an investigative agency at the present moment.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: How would the officers of the new department be trained in law enforcement techniques?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will SPRING Singapore draw learnings from any other consumer protection agencies in developed countries which have a long track record of operation?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Sixth, how would SPRING Singapore approach the issue of offshore online retailers who may not have a legal entity in Singapore and where legal action in the Courts may thus be problematic?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Such retailers can be expected to take up a larger share of e-tailing revenues in the future as new platforms emerge to connect not only large vendors but also mid-sized vendors in countries like Japan, Korea, the US and Australia with Singapore consumers?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I wonder if there is a role here for an international consumer protection and enforcement network.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This may be necessary to create a stronger deterrent against those who are egregious offenders and who feel that they can prey on certain vulnerable and captive groups of customers.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Including MLM under this framework will help the legitimate MLM industry to protect its reputation, to grow and to contribute to the economy.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: We are one of the world's top destinations for luxury retailers, attracting luxury and business fashion brands worldwide.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: So, our retail and F&B industry is a thriving and important component in our economy.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: It is also noteworthy that many tourists come to Singapore to enjoy shopping besides visiting the various tourist attractions.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: Our retail industry is very much inherent in the Singapore brand.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: We need to not only give good service but also be honest and above board in our dealings with customers, be they local or foreign.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: Last year, we saw how the years of hard work put in by everyone in the retail industry and STB were thrown to the dumps, thanks to the reckless, irresponsible and condemnable action of an errant retailer and his staff at Sim Lim Square.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs even put up a notice on its website warning Chinese citizens to be careful or even avoid going to Sim Lim Square, following a series of fraudulent and unethical sales tactics by a few miscreants that caught the headlines in the world press.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: As a consequence, the mall also suffered from the negative publicity.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: I applaud the Government's effort for taking this matter seriously and giving SPRING Singapore more teeth to protect the consumers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: While the new initiatives are commendable, I think it may have left a gap in that there are companies, especially those in the gym, spa and beauty care sector, which are in the practice of selling packages to the public.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: They seek advanced payments and lure, or sometimes coerce, customers to sign up for six-month or even 12-month packages.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: Many consumers would be hard put to recover their money.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: We are looking at a franchise that has been in operation for about a decade and was supposedly an established industry player.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: Customers took them in good faith in buying prepaid packages, only to find themselves locked out without prior warning.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: Surely, the management knew they were going belly up and yet they did not stop the sales staff from recruiting.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: This is doing something to defraud the consumers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: There is a CaseTrust for the spa, beauty and wellness industry.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: Prior to this year, it seems that CASE has received a number of complaints against California Fitness.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: Surely this should have served as a red flag.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: Additionally, I hope SPRING Singapore would pay more attention to companies that have had complaints lodged against them and, depending on the severity of the situation, possibly suspend them from selling prepaid services, or put out a warning sign to the public.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: It is like what the stock exchange does to flag out listed companies which are showing a sudden run-up in prices or put companies on the restricted trading list.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: Allow me to summarise the above two points in Chinese.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   Retail and service sectors are two important contributors to our economy.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: From the Sim Lim Square incident, we can see that one unscrupulous retailer is enough to damage the reputation of Singapore.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: Therefore, I strongly support the amendment to the Act to confer powers on SPRING Singapore to investigate and penalise unscrupulous retailers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: I would also like to highlight another service that many consumers have grumbles about and that is prepaid packages.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: For example, California Fitness was recently bankrupted and yet, before they closed down, they continued to sell many packages.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: I hope that the Government can consider legislation to require those who sell prepaid packages such as Page: 84 gyms, beauty salons, and spas, to be accredited by CaseTrust.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: Should there be many consumers complaining against them, SPRING Singapore can take preventive measures by temporarily barring them from selling prepaid packages.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: (In English): Ultimately, prevention is better than cure and I hope that in cases of poor business practices, the problems can be nipped in the bud before a large number of people are implicated.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: In the case of Sim Lim Square, the mall's management subsequently did a good job working closely with the authorities to weed out the other errant retailers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: It would be good if SPRING Singapore could keep in close touch with various retail watchdogs and organisations to identify problematic retail practices in advance.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: Next, while I note that we are giving more bite to look into cases to protect consumers, I hope the Minister can clarify why the investigation may be carried out by an Auxiliary Police Officer, appointed under the Police Force Act, instead of the regular Police.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: I do not know if this will help to expedite investigations.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: I do not know if these officers have been involved in investigation work previously and have sufficient experience to do the task.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: On the flip side, if SPRING Singapore has its own investigation officers, would they be given sufficient training and the confidence to engage the culprits as some of these errant retailers can be gangsters?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
text: Otherwise, they may end up like some Land Transport Authority officers who got into scuffles and tiffs when trying to carry out their duties.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This diversity enhances the attractiveness of Singapore to locals and visitors alike as a place to live, work and play.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Given its impact on our economy and reputation, it is essential that our retail industry engages in sound business practices.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: An effective and responsive consumer protection framework helps to provide this check and balance.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, I fully support the amendments to the CPFTA Bill tabled today.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They are timely changes to strengthen our consumer protection framework by increasing the measures which may be taken against the few egregious players to maintain a high level of trust in our retail sector.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry has explained that it is important for consumers to know their rights and be alert to what unfair trading practices are, to be in a good position to make sound purchasing decisions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Indeed, this principle of "caveat emptor", or "let the buyer beware" must continue as the key plank of our consumer protection framework.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: To be able to make an informed purchasing decision, consumers need to know their rights as consumers and know what to look out for, including questions to ask the retailer before making a purchase.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I was very happy to hear from my resident, Mr Choo Ming Yong, 69 years old.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: He is an avid photographer who recently bought a camera worth about $3,000.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: He checked out different retailers to compare the prices of the model he was interested in and he also noted the warranty terms and period before finally deciding on his purchase.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This practice, he told me, has resulted in him being a happier consumer, who is more satisfied with his current buy than the previous Page: 85 camera purchases a few years back.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For Mr Choo, being more aware as a consumer paid off.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am, therefore, strongly of the view that even as we strengthen the CPFTA, our efforts on the consumer education front must also continue.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: When consumers are knowledgeable, alert and aware they can make better and informed purchasing decisions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: To this end, CASE plays a key role in championing consumer education and raising consumer awareness.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: MTI has worked with CASE on broad-based initiatives and targeted efforts to reach more vulnerable consumer segments, for example the elderly, based on their specific concerns.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The talks will teach consumers what they should look out for when making purchases, especially for products and services that have attracted high volume of complaints, like for the consumers to read and understand the terms of conditions of the deal before entering into a transaction.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I urge CASE to explore new channels to educate consumers and build consumer awareness, especially in areas where we are seeing more issues faced by consumers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There are signposts to guide consumers in their purchases.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For example, accreditation schemes for businesses like CaseTrust ensures fair trading practices and greater protection for consumers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We encourage more businesses to take part in these schemes as it not only demonstrates their fair trading practices, it also sets them apart from their competitors.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Beyond that businesses may go further by volunteering to provide prepayment protection if they collect advance payments from consumers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They may do so by purchasing business insurance, which is already available for spa wellness, fitness and renovation sectors.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We will continue to encourage consumers to patronise accredited businesses that provide protection for prepayments.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: By doing so, consumers also send a signal that practices are welcome, and more businesses will come onboard to be accredited.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Even as such steps are in place, we need the cooperation of the consumer to be armed with the right information, to stay alert against errant sellers or service providers and be aware of their rights so as to make informed purchasing decisions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As the saying goes, prevention is better than cure.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: An informed, alert, and aware consumer is the best defence.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Mandarin):   Deputy Speaker, Parliamentary colleagues, we all know that the fundamental of doing business is trust.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Only when you are honest and trustworthy can your business last.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In an era where information is widely available, a few errant businesses cheating consumers for short-term gains will not only cause losses for the consumers but also sully the reputation of the entire retail and service industry.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: CPFTA is to send a strong message to these black sheep that they must not cheat consumers and damage the reputation of the retail and service industry.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As the saying goes, "If you hurt others, you will end up hurting yourself".

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: A small number of errant businesses is enough to ruin Singapore's reputation as a shopping paradise, and the consequence can be dire.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is very important and beneficial to the development of our retail and service industry.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They should not easily believe those promotions that sound too good to be true and avoid falling into a trap.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We all have a role to play to uphold trust in society.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I hope that retailers, industry leaders and consumers can all treat CPFTA seriously and understand the meaning and spirit behind it.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We must continue to uphold the highest standard so that Singapore can continue to be an attractive place for leisure, shopping, work, travel and personal development.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Importantly, there must be effort to empower consumers by creating awareness and educating them on how consumers can potentially fall for the gimmicks of unscrupulous retailers, even though such retailers may be far and few in numbers.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: We need to ensure the rights of the consumers are preserved and the principles of fair trade are embraced by retailers and also those in the e-commerce businesses.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Sim Lim Square, Lucky Plaza and People's Park Complex are some places well-known for all the wrong reasons where consumers, both locals and tourists, had had distasteful experiences in purchases.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: While we take precautions to protect those consumers from retailers who mislead or misrepresent information pertaining to the products, equal efforts should be made to protect the interests of consumers who make their purchases both in person, through third party or electronically as our e-commerce trading is also growing fast in this highly connected place.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: It is important that we assure both locals and tourists that the products they buy are of good quality, improving the image of Singapore as a "shoppers' paradise" and not "shoppers' nightmare".

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: For instance, the introduction of lemon laws protects consumers against defective goods that fail to conform to contract or meet satisfactory quality or performance standards at the time of purchase for a specified duration of time.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Likewise, I would urge that any review and changes to the consumer laws should raise consumers' awareness of errant retailers as to who they are and where they are located so as to protect consumers' interests, especially against such errant retailers who persists in unfair trading practices and continue to violate the injunction orders.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: However, I would like to seek five clarifications on the Bill.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Explanation of the following, "retailer charging a price for goods or services that is substantially higher than an estimate provided to the consumer, except where a consumer has agreed to a higher price in advance".

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: What if the retailer is charging a much higher price due to quality of service or something else?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: What if a consumer has agreed to purchase under undue pressure or coercion as he/she perceives it to be?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Can the affected consumer raise this to be an unfair sales tactic employed by the retailer?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: In this aspect, consumers, especially from a vulnerable group, must be protected and understand what difference in quality means.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: The affected consumers, who may be the complainants, must be educated on the consumers' rights and protection and how they can potentially prevent this from recurring.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Retailers under injunction, too, must be made to attend compulsory retailing ethics sessions.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Two, regulations, section 20(2)(c), on controlling or prohibiting any practice in relation to any consumer transaction.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: If the errant owner starts a similar business with the same wrongful tactic, does section 20(2)(c) include a restriction based on the registered owner of business or supplier?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: If the errant owner embarks in other businesses applying the same wrongful tactics, is the said section applied to other businesses of the same registered owner?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Three, section 6, consumer's right to sue for unfair practices.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Will there be stronger deterrence for unfair sales practices?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Four, perishables and consumables are covered, with the presumption that defects reported within six months existing at the point of delivery will only apply up to the normal shelf life of the perishable or consumable, if the shelf life is less than six months.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: What happens if the consumer consumes or partially consumes the goods?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: The recent petition for refund for Jay Chou concert tickets due to poor sound quality is one such example.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: If an individual was to lodge a complaint against the concert organiser, is the Act applicable?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: There is an increasing number of online transactions, including the rise of online service providers, such as Deliveroo, Foodpanda and so on.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Is the Bill applicable to complaints against online service providers, such as Deliveroo and Foodpanda food delivery and so on?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Does the Bill also cover online selling or consumer-to-consumer transactions, such as Carousell shopping?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Does this Bill cover e-commerce retail businesses and purchases?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Will the third party or middleman facilitating the sale be liable if the consumer complains?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Examples of such middlemen include 65daigou, ezbuy, Qoo10 and Shopee, who buy and sell on mobile.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: First, consumers to be able to call a hotline number to report immediately should they experience any unfair consumer trading practices which they manage to avoid or even potential acts which they hear of so that the administering agent can record and investigate on this matter, Page: 88 especially when the number of alerts for the same retailer shows a rising trend.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: This acts as prevention, in addition to deterrent measures.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: In the programme, we must reinforce the positive, too, and make them realise that fair trading practices will enhance their business reputation and help sustain their business.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I draw attention to three specific areas of the amendment Bill which can be further elucidated.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: First, with reference to sections 9(4)(a), (b) and (c), the intention of these sections is to make it known to the public and potential consumers that there has been a declaration issued, or an injunction granted against the supplier for having engaged, is engaged or is likely to engage in an unfair practice.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: The actions required in these sections are thorough.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
