text: However, can I suggest two much simpler ways that can be included if the intent of these provisions is to make it publicly known that a declaration had been issued, or an injunction had been granted against the supplier?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: This would also make it easier for STB to check for compliance with the publication requirement.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Does "individual" include a sole proprietor and anyone else who supplies goods without having a registered business?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: With more and more people doing online shopping with overseas suppliers, some have taken advantage of this by becoming so-called "agents" to assist local buyers, especially when the websites are in foreign languages.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Customers pay these "agents" a fee for procuring items for them.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: The "agents" will source for the desired items and translate the description of the items into English.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: All transactions are between the customers and the "agents".

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: For sections 9(8) and 9(9), again, a distinction is made between "supplier" and "individual".

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: However, why is a distinction now made between "supplier" and "individual"?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Does "individual" have the same meaning as for sections 9(4)(e) and (f) and again in sections 10(6)(C) Page: 89 and 10(9)?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Third, in section 9(10), the only penalty here is the extension of the specified period.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: But is this sufficient to deter the supplier or individual from non-compliance?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: If the recalcitrant supplier or individual has reached the last few years of the specified period, he can wilfully choose not to comply with any orders, knowing that it would be only another one or two years till the end of the specified period and nothing else would be done against him.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: What if there had already been an earlier extension of the specified period to 10 years and the supplier or individual did not comply with the order under the above sections?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Does this provision mean that there can be a further extension of the specified period to more than 10 years?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: How many extensions of the specified period can there be?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: (In Mandarin):   The amendments are a positive and welcome step towards greater protection of consumers.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: First, set up a one-stop centre or hotline so that consumers can easily report unfair practices.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Second, enforcement against those "black sheep" retailers should be targeted and robust.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: (In English): To conclude, the amendments are a positive step towards greater protection of consumers.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I suggest that a one-stop centre, both physical and virtual, and a hotline for aggrieved customers be set up.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In the same vein, enforcement against rogue businesses and traders should be speedy, resolute and robust.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: This is so that consumers can be better protected and not left in the lurch.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: SPRING Singapore must take ownership with its new powers.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In short, I hope these questions and suggestions can be addressed for greater clarity and effectiveness.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am certain that consumers will welcome the proposed changes, as it would level the playing field between them and errant retailers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Honest and ethical retailers will also welcome the stronger deterrent measures that will be taken against the minority "black sheep" among their industries.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Some tourism websites even had comments warning others to be careful when purchasing electronic goods from the mall.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Some comments went as far as to say, "Be careful when you buy things from Singapore".

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is heartening to note that the Bill will empower SPRING Singapore to gather evidence, file injunction applications with the Courts against persistent errant retailers and enforce Page: 90 compliance with injunction orders.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This sends a strong signal to retailers that there is someone with teeth keeping an eye out for unfair trading practices.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Consumers will be able to shop with greater ease, knowing that action can and will be taken by SPRING Singapore against those who persist in taking advantage of consumers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Courts may also require the retailers to inform the administering agency of any changes in employment involving consumer transactions to prevent them from sidestepping injunction orders by setting up new entities.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Such a measure will only be effective if there are regular spot checks conducted on the ground against errant retailers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: SPRING Singapore must also impose stricter penalties on those who persistently flout the Court orders.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I would also like to urge SPRING Singapore and CASE to place greater emphasis on public education.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In order for people to shop at ease, they must be aware of their rights as consumers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many, especially the elderly, foreign workers and tourists, may not have adequate knowledge about their rights as consumers and they are the ones most likely to fall prey to unethical and errant retailers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Information about consumer rights and unethical business practices should be made readily available on both traditional and digital media.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is only when all consumers are armed with information about their rights will they be able to prevent themselves from being victim to a dishonest retailer.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In fact, we can all play a part in generating public awareness about consumer rights and ethical business practices.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The proliferation of technology and social media allows us to come together as a community to share our "first-person" experiences, both the good and the bad.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This enhances awareness among consumers, and retailers will inadvertently be pushed towards delivering positive service experiences and providing quality products to every customer.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: After all, satisfied customers can become powerful brand ambassadors.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The first pertains to consumers who are the initial victims of an errant retailer.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Under the revised Act, potential consumers would benefit from the injunction orders as it allows them to steer clear of the errant retailers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But what about the victims in the first instances?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Cost and complexity of process are often reasons given by victims for their reluctance in pursuing compensation.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My second concern is whether the revised Act covers online retailers, both registered and unregistered entities.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Currently, it seems like the Act is only able to act on brick-and-mortar retailers, which does not reflect the current landscape of the retail sector.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: More can be done to better protect the interests of customers of businesses that abruptly close.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is a common practice among fitness centres and beauty salons to sell "lifetime memberships" and packages spanning several years.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Thousands of dollars are paid upfront before any services or products are utilised.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Even when the company undergoes liquidation, the chances of customers getting their money back are remote.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For many victims, legal avenues are the only way that they could possibly be able to get some of their money back, so laws should be strengthened to protect them, regardless of whether the Page: 91 transaction is with an online or a brick-and-mortar retailer.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: If the Minister could share some thoughts on whether there are any upcoming plans to address these issues, it would be much appreciated.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It serves to keep errant retailers in check, which will, hopefully, enhance our nation's reputation as a retail and shopping haven.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, consumers are still vulnerable against errant retailers, and I urge for more to be done to address this disparity.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The events in the last 12 months have seen a clamour for tighter laws so that the likes of Jover and others like him would not resurface to haunt innocent shoppers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I can still recall the pitiful look of the Vietnamese tourist who begged for the return of his money from the shop.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We must come down hard on such operators.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, speed is of the essence in any investigation.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I hope, with the passage of this Bill, the authorities will be able to move more expeditiously so that the errant retailers can be dealt with swiftly and expeditiously and those who are wronged can get early redress.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In taking on this additional role, I believe SPRING Singapore will see to it that its investigation team is backed up with the infrastructure to ensure that they are able to carry out their duties.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Investigation work, as many of us may not realise, is more than just acting on complaints and recording statements.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is also about collating evidence and often this requires some strategising, maybe even surveillance work, so that the culprits can be caught with some element of surprise.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: While I know it will tap on the resources of the Auxiliary Police Force, there should also be a team of officers from SPRING Singapore who can coordinate and liaise with the field officers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The work of the officers will be keenly followed by the public and I hope they will rise to the occasion when the time comes.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: People work hard, earn more and spend more.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As a result, more and more of these issues arise between consumers and retailers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am sometimes at a loss as to why, despite much publicity, consumers are still taken in by glib-tongued marketers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For Page: 92 example, the timeshare industry was in the limelight with numerous complaints being lodged to CASE by people who were cheated.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Often, the victims would be lured with offers of being the lucky ones to win prizes, or specially selected in a draw, or the often-used trick of stopping someone to say, "Today is your lucky day and you are selected" and so on.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Many horror stories appeared in the media year after year, yet we still get people duped into various schemes.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have, from time to time, also seen a few residents of mine, housewives and retirees with families, become victims of these.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Another nagging area I would like to raise is the question of online trading practices.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Besides travel, the other most common purchases are fashion, lifestyle and food products as well as services.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We are in an era where we are more reliant on technology for everything that we want.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: While technology may make it more efficient in the execution of a process, it often leaves gaps and many questions unanswered at times.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is quite impossible to seek clarification under such circumstances and replies are often less than satisfactory.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Today, we have colourful and interactive websites selling products and services online.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The sellers post photos, drawings, all kinds of media gimmicks, littered with superlatives.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But what you see therein may not necessarily be what they actually represent.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am aware that there is such a thing as a "return policy" for online shopping but this is not the norm.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Buyers are at the mercy of sellers who find it perfectly acceptable to not offer a return or exchange policy.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If they do, they would indicate, but in small print.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, you make the click and add it to your cart and you are off to spending good money for bad.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Also, in the case of errant online retailers, how will injunction orders be enforced?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Worse, some online transactions are cross-border, so it probably creates some issues with the voluntary nature of publicising injunction orders on foreign-based websites.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In Malay):   Next, can I ask if pre-owned goods are covered by this amendment to the law?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This can cover anything from bicycles, musical instruments to old furniture and antiques.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Some people buy used goods not because they cannot afford new ones, but because they would like certain older designs that have a classic look.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I hope the Minister can consider a provision where the buyer can ask for repairs or replacement of the product if it is misrepresented to the buyer.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And, if this still cannot result in an acceptable resolution to the dispute, the buyer can choose to keep the goods but with a price reduction.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The third option is to be able to return the item and get a full refund.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This practice is especially prevalent in the healthcare and fitness industry and I feel that we should nip this problem in the bud rather than allow the public to continue to be fleeced by unscrupulous operators.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Often, the operators know that their ship is sinking yet they failed to inform their staff to stop signing on more customers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In English): Lastly, we are in an age where scams are quite prevalent.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Otherwise, the spread of word via WhatsApp, e-forums, Facebook and so on may go unnoticed and people are also wary of believing whether what was posted was true or just a prank.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: At the end of the day, I feel that there is so much that the authorities can do but as consumers, we too must be vigilant and do not fall for the freebies and other gimmicks.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: We have a reputation for clean Government and clean business practices, by and large.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: We stand for the rule of law, which means that when there is misconduct, when there is fraud, we take firm action.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Trust is also a competitive advantage for any economy, especially advanced economies which can no longer compete on being the lowest cost venue alone.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: But when there is a shortage of trust, consumers become afraid, consumers are worried, customers become scared.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Some might say, "Let the buyer beware", or, in Latin, "caveat emptor".

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: In a market with too little trust, buyers are fearful – caveat emptor becomes "timet emptor".

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Instead of "Let the buyer beware", it becomes "Let the buyer be afraid".

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Or to put it another way, without adequate safeguards, caveat emptor can become "bo cheng hu", if Mr Deputy Speaker will allow me to use the vernacular.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: When the market is short on trust, consumers miss out on potentially good offers, while sellers miss out on potential sales.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Trust is also a shared common good for the whole community.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: In a shopping mall, the whole business community benefits when the mall has a good reputation collectively for honourable merchants and shop owners.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: But there is also the problem of freeloaders and, in particular, what I will call "reputation polluters" – shops which treat consumers badly and unfairly, making unfair profits, polluting the reputation of neighbouring businesses and the entire mall.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: And, as we have seen in the past, dishonourable operators evading legal injunctions by changing the name of the company, finding proxies.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: But I wonder if there is room for the Ministry to go further.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: There have been cases in the media involving prepaid packages, where consumers pay a significant amount upfront for goods or services which have yet to be provided.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Deputy Speaker, in a fair and just society, we need to protect the people.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The law and the law enforcement agencies have a very important role.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Page: 94 The modern economy brings international challenges and international competition.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Goods and services in developing countries are cheaper than ours.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Therefore, in the 21st century market, Singapore's competitive advantages include skills, science and technology and reputation.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: It is worth our effort to cultivate and protect the trust of travellers and consumers in our market, our shops and department stores.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: We must stay vigilant and not let a few black sheep ruin the collective reputation of an industry or sully our national reputation.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: (In English): Let me now end in English.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Step by step, Mr Deputy Speaker, progressive policies help us build a fairer and more just society.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: And for these reasons, I stand in support of this Bill.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Some Members have raised pertinent points which I will now address.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The current Unfair Practice No 20 in the Second Schedule of the CPFTA already provides that retailers have to make material information clear to consumers prior to transactions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is important that consumers read, understand and agree to the terms and conditions before making the purchase.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Consumers do have a choice to walk away from the transaction if they think that the terms and conditions are unfair or overly onerous and this is where consumer education plays an important role in helping consumers to understand what the terms they are signing up for mean to them.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Ms K Thanaletchimi asked if it is an unfair practice for the retailer to put undue pressure or coercion on the consumer.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: A consumer who encounters such an unfair practice may provide feedback to, and seek assistance from, CASE to obtain redress from the retailer concerned.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Ms Thanaletchimi also may wish to know that CASE has already been actively educating consumers on pressure-selling tactics and what consumers should look out for.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Ms Thanaletchimi also raised a question about what if the retailer is charging a much higher price due to the quality of service and so on.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Well, the term in the Bill did say that a retailer charging a price for goods or services that is substantially higher than the estimate provided to the consumer, except where the consumer has agreed to a higher price in advance.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This means that Page: 95 the consumer must believe that the higher than estimated quoted price is good value for money.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is a reflection of the diversity of our retail landscape, as retailers are constantly thinking of new ideas, good ways to attract and to serve customers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Pre-payments are, in themselves, a common business practice worldwide and it is not necessarily unfair or illegal as a practice.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: When offering a prepaid package, businesses generally do offer customers a discount.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, in many ways, consumers do benefit from such prepayment schemes.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: These schemes are not actually harmful to consumers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But the fact that there is such a wide range of choices for consumers makes it even more important for consumers to exercise their choices carefully, particularly when it comes to very large purchases, very large amounts of prepayments or very long durations of contract periods.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Even large businesses that have been operational for many years, such as California Fitness, are not immune to business failure.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Therefore, it is important, as I emphasised earlier, for consumers to make informed purchasing decisions and consider if there are possible risks involved in such a transaction and what is their own capacity to bear losses under such contractual terms.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Such measures may affect the cost of doing business which would eventually be passed on to consumers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Overseas jurisdictions, including those in the European Union, Australia and Hong Kong, also recognise the challenges and do not impose broad-based measures against prepayment per se.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Currently, over 800 businesses are CaseTrust-accredited, as Ms Low Yen Ling alluded to earlier.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We encourage more businesses to sign up and to go further by voluntarily providing prepayment protection if they collect advanced prepayments from their customers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But in this regard, customers do play a role.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As Ms Low Yen Ling said earlier, customers are encouraged to purchase from such retailers because by doing so, customers send a very strong and very clear signal that such good practices are welcomed, and more retailers will come onboard because they do want to have a good word of mouth to attract more customers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Retailers can also differentiate themselves from their competitors by making themselves commit to CaseTrust accreditation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The Singapore Vehicle Traders Association and the Singapore Jewellers Association, for example, have both done so.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: LEAD funding will co-fund the associations' cost of developing, administering and promoting accreditation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It will also co-fund the members' cost of signing up for CaseTrust accreditation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Of Page: 96 course, CASE and SPRING Singapore, as forward-facing agencies, are engaging constantly with trade associations and can also take the opportunities to reach out to these associations and their businesses to educate the businesses on what constitutes fair or unfair practices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In reply to Mr Leon Perera's question earlier about how we go about educating businesses on what are fair and unfair practices, let me just bring Members back to my earlier opening speech about us having a whole spectrum of incremental measures to try and educate our consumers and prevent egregious behaviour.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: By the time we have put up an injunction, usually, it means that CASE would have received a certain number of complaints from consumers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It would not be as if one customer made a complaint about a practice for business and we start investigating and putting in injunctions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Usually, by the time SPRING Singapore comes in to look at the possibility of a need for injunction and starts to do investigation, CASE would probably have received numerous complaints and through that process, there will be a discussion with the businesses, educating them that what they do is not right, there will be a mediation process and negotiation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Then, there will be a call for VCAs to be signed with the businesses.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Through this whole process, businesses which may have inadvertently flouted the rules or engaged in unfair practices will have a chance to review their own business practices and decide to change.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: These are processes which will flag out businesses that may have inadvertently entered into unfair practices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The whole spectrum of measures allows us to filter out businesses for education in that sense.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Again, as I have said, CASE and SPRING Singapore will continue to engage the trade associations.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: SPRING Singapore will work with CASE to publicise the injunction actions taken and the injunction orders obtained against these errant retailers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This will raise consumers' awareness of errant retailers who are under injunctions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: SPRING Singapore will also monitor the activities of the businesses and individuals under injunctions to ensure that they comply with these injunction orders.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Mr Melvin Yong, Mr Patrick Tay and I believe Ms Thanalatchimi as well have asked if the CPFTA protects consumers who make online purchases of goods and services and how an e-commerce business which is served with an injunction would publicise the fact that it is under an injunction if it is ordered to do so by the Courts.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This approach is aligned with consumer protection in Australia and Hong Kong where actions have been taken against errant online retailers under the main consumer protection legislations.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To ensure that consumers are actually made aware of them being under an injunction, the Courts may also require them to notify the consumer in writing and to obtain the consumers' written acknowledgement of the notice before any transactions can be finalised.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: SPRING Singapore, as the administering agency for CPFTA, will work with CASE to publicise the list of businesses, including e-commerce businesses, which are under any injunction order.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The Page: 97 administering agency will also monitor the activities of these businesses to ensure that they are in compliance with the injunction orders.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Patrick Tay and Ms Thanaletchimi also asked if agents who act as middlemen to assist local consumers to purchase from foreign websites are considered as suppliers under the CPFTA.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Under the CPFTA, a person is considered to be a supplier if the person engages in an activity with the intent of carrying on a business.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This means that the transaction must be one of several transactions, that you are not just doing it one-off.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: If you are my friend and we decide to buy something from each other, then that is a one-off thing, that is not necessarily a business transaction.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But if you carry on several transactions, either with the same consumers or with other consumers, then you are deemed as being a supplier.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat raised the issue of overseas e-commerce retailers and how orders to publish the injunction may be enforced on them.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Leon Perera also asked about e-commerce retailers as well and made the point that the proliferation and increasing popularity of online shopping mean that there will be more such online transactions taking place.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But the reality is that such online transactions may also be cross-border in nature, where it may not be possible to enforce the judgment against an overseas retailer, especially if he has no presence in Singapore at all.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Therefore, this brings us back to the important principle of caveat emptor where we have emphasised many times that consumer education is the key principle undergirding the entire consumer protection framework.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Consumers need to be made more aware of the risk of purchasing from overseas online retailers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The issue of enforcement against overseas parties is a practical jurisdictional issue, which is not necessarily unique to Singapore.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Consumers must, therefore, exercise judgement in any form of transactions, especially online ones.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Today, there are many online reviews about the reputation of websites and the reliability of transactions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Consumers should use some of these reviews from fellow consumers online to get a sense of what they are going into before they make purchases from websites.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The National Council on Crime Prevention also has a website at www.scamalert.sg, where scammers and scam sites are listed and where consumers can also alert and educate themselves.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Yee Chia Hsing asked if SPRING Singapore can publish a blacklist of errant renovation contractors.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The details that may be published will include the name of the entity or the individual, if it is a sole proprietorship, and the business address as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: SPRING Singapore will monitor the activities of the businesses and individuals under injunction to ensure that they comply with these injunction orders.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked about how customers will be notified about businesses or individuals under injunction.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Ms Thanaletchimi and Mr Patrick Tay suggested that injunction orders be publicised through prominent displays of the injunction notice at the shop premises and errant retailers' website to raise consumer awareness.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And in filing an injunction Page: 98 application against errant business with the Courts, SPRING Singapore, as the administering agency for the CPFTA, may specify the manner in which the errant businesses may be required to publicise the injunction orders.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This could include notices to be put up by the errant businesses in their shop premises.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It could be a notice or on its own business website as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This may be in addition to other forms of publicising to ensure prompt and adequate publicity of the injunction order.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Melvin Yong suggested SPRING Singapore impose stricter penalties on those who persistently flout injunction orders.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Patrick Tay suggested that the specified period for compliance with the additional measures be extended beyond 10 years for recalcitrant retailers who do not comply with the requirements for the full specified period.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is a criminal offence which could result in a fine or together with imprisonment.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: SPRING Singapore, as administering agency for the CPFTA, may take the errant retailer to Court for contempt of Court.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: SPRING Singapore can also apply to the Courts to increase the duration of the requirements for the errant retailer to publicise the injunction order, notify consumers of the injunction and inform SPRING Singapore of changes of the errant retailer's status.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The CPFTA also provides for the Minister to prescribe changes to the specified periods that the Courts may order for compliance with the additional measures.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Ms Thanaletchimi asked if the Bill will restrict an errant retailer under injunction from starting a new business and persisting with the errant unfair practice.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Ms Thanaletchimi suggested that all retailers, including those under injunction, attend courses on how to engage in fair trading.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: There are already such courses available, and some are initiated by the retailers themselves.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For example, the Sim Lim Square Management Committee tied up with Nanyang Polytechnic to train the mall retailers in areas, such as improving interactions with customers and how to maintain a professional image.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We encourage more retailers and operators to do the same because this will help them differentiate themselves from their competitors.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Patrick Tay asked about the distinction between a supplier and an individual.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The distinction is to provide for injunction action to be taken not just against errant business entities but also against errant individuals.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This overcomes a challenge in the current CPFTA in which errant individuals side-step the injunction orders given to the businesses by closing their businesses, setting up a new business using a different person's name and then continue to persist in unfair practices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan asked if stringent enforcement could exacerbate the challenges faced by businesses, especially during weak economic times.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In the grand scheme of things, this is a very small number, compared to the majority of retailers in Singapore who do not engage in unfair practice and, in fact, are interested to do an honest business.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Retailers Page: 99 who do not carry out unfair trading businesses, therefore, should have nothing to worry about as far as stringent enforcement is concerned.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Enforcement actions should not impact the majority, unless you are engaged in unfair practices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: CASE and STB will assist consumers to resolve their disputes with businesses and obtain redress through negotiation, mediation and VCAs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I hope that the strengthening of the injunction will move more cases towards the front end of the spectrum, that is, towards education, awareness, mediation and VCAs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, this should send a signal to businesses which are even contemplating engaging in egregious behaviour to stop immediately and to go into voluntary compliance.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, we hope to move cases more into the front end, into the preventive aspects of retail behaviour but, if so required, Police action will be taken against criminal behaviour.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah also asked why Auxiliary Police Officers instead of regular Police Officers will work with SPRING Singapore to investigate errant retailers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Er Dr Lee and Mr Saktiandi Supaat have highlighted that SPRING Singapore's officers need to be trained to carry out investigation and enforcement work.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The appointment of Auxiliary Police Officers to undertake investigation is not unique to the CPFTA.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As I have mentioned earlier, it also does not mean that the Police will not investigate if the errant businesses engage in activities that are criminalised under the Penal Code.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: SPRING Singapore will refer such cases to the Police to investigate.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This ensures that only cases that require definite Police action will be referred to the Police, so as not to overstretch the bandwidth of the Police.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Page: 100 SPRING Singapore, whose existing mandate today is to oversee the growth of enterprises in Singapore, will balance this need for enforcement and its expanded role as the administering agency for the CPFTA to ensure businesses' interests are also adequately looked after.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked about clauses 12(i) and 12(j) and the power to enter premises.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But in that case, as clause 12(i) has specified, there will be a two days' notice given to the retailer so that they are notified that there will be action taken on the premises of the retailer.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is not something that is a default position.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Clause 12(k) also provides how items that are taken during the search are to be handled so that the interests of the retailer, whose items may have been taken as evidence can be protected as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As Mr Patrick Tay called for earlier, he is looking for speedy, resolute and robust action from SPRING Singapore.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This clause allows us to act much quicker against retailers who have engaged in extreme egregious activities.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As I have said earlier, by the time we have invoked the investigation powers of SPRING Singapore towards filing an injunction, there would have been evidence from engagement through CASE, multiple retailers and feedback from consumers about this egregious behaviour of the retailer, so that such sufficient evidence from the sheer number of people who have been complaining and the evidence that is gathered by CASE, to allow us to get a sense of what is the urgency of the case at hand, for SPRING Singapore to invoke such powers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I hope that clarifies the question raised by Mr Dennis Tan.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Leon Perera asked about the provisions for tourists who have disputes with errant retailers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Those who do not wish to appear in person at SCT or are unable to remain in Singapore until their cases are heard have the option to assigning CASE to represent their case on their behalf at SCT.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is provided for under the SCT Act.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about what is being done to help tourists and foreign nationals to avoid falling prey to errant retailers who engage in unfair practices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: STB has worked with CASE and the Police to develop a brochure with advice on the precautionary measures that visitors should take when purchasing electronic products in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This brochure is distributed at Sim Lim Square and other key touch points such as the Singapore Business Centre at the Orchard Gateway and STB's office at Tourism Court.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Consumer protection advisories with smart shopping tips, such as checking of receipts and invoices are also available on the STB's website yoursingapore.com.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Zainal Sapari has asked if the administering agency will take injunction action against timeshare businesses which engage in unfair trading practices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Timeshare businesses, like all businesses that engage in transactions with consumers, are required to engage in fair trading practices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Errant businesses, including those in the timeshare sector which persist in unfair trading practices, may be investigated and have injunctions taken against them be SPRING Singapore, the administering agency for the CPFTA.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: If they are Page: 101 handed injunction orders by the Courts, then they are required to comply with the requirements which SPRING Singapore will enforce.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In 2015, timeshare, as a problem, has dropped out of the top 10 sectors with the most complaints to CASE.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This will augment ongoing consumer education initiatives to enable consumers to make informed purchasing decisions, such as being aware of scammers and their tactics.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Business models can change, consumer shopping patterns may also evolve.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, it is not always possible to use legislation to cover all manner of consumer actions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Consumers, therefore, need to be prudent and exercise discretion and judgement in their transactions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Therefore, as I said many times before, consumer education will remain the key pillar of our consumer protection framework.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: SPRING Singapore and CASE will work together on consumer education after the Bill is passed.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As the administering agency, SPRING Singapore will put up information on the legislative changes and the list of frequently asked questions on their webpage to help consumers better understand the changes.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: SPRING Singapore will work with CASE to publicise information on errant businesses which have been issued injunction orders by the Courts, and CASE will also disseminate information on the changes to the Act at its upcoming events and outreach activities, such as consumer education advertisements, on toggle.sg.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: On questions of redress for consumers, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Leon Perera asked for compensation for consumers who were affected by the unfair practices of errant retailers before an injunction was taken.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: CASE and STB will remain the first point of contact for locals and tourists and assist consumers with their disputes with retailers, including obtaining redress of compensation through negotiation, mediation and VCAs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Consumers also can take civil action via SCT.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked if pre-owned goods are covered by the CPFTA and if so, the forms of redress that consumers can ask for if the retailers have misrepresented the goods to the consumer.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Second-hand goods are covered by the lemon law or the additional consumer rights in respect of non-conforming goods as stated in the CPFTA.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: However, what constitutes satisfactory quality would need to take into account the good's age at the time of delivery and the price that is paid.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is to be fair to the retailers as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: If the cost of the remedy demanded by the consumer is disproportionate in comparison, then the retailer may offer one of the alternative remedies provided for in the legislation, such as a reduction in price or returning the product for a refund.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As per existing laws, the refunded amount may be reduced to take into account the use that the consumer had of the goods they have received.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Ms Thanaletchimi asked how the Bill when passed will apply if perishables and consumables, which are covered by the Bill up to the normal shelf life of the consumable or perishable, are consumed or partially consumed by the consumer.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To the extent that the item comes in a package, Page: 102 the consumer can seek recourse from the retailer or for a replacement if it can be ascertained either from what remains of the partially consumed product or by some other means that the item had failed to meet satisfactory quality within its normal shelf life.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The consumer may ask for a refund if the retailer does not replace the item.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Dr Koh, can you hold on for a while, while I move for the extension.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I was hoping you would end before 7.00 pm.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Ms Thanaletchimi also asked if poor sound quality at a concert is covered by the Bill.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Services, such as a concert performance, are not covered as the remedies under the lemon law regime are tailored for goods and are generally inappropriate for services.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For example, it is quite impossible to return the service once it has been rendered.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: On multi-level marketing (MLM), Ms Thanaletchimi and Mr Leon Perera asked if the Bill applies to MLM.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To conclude, Deputy Speaker, Sir, in looking at enhancing consumer protection I want to remind Members that we should not lose sight of the fact that most retailers are reasonable and most consumers are actually sensible.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The amendments to the Act enhance the protection of consumers against the small number of errant retailers who persist in unfair practices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is also pro-business, as it avoids imposing widespread compliance burdens on a majority of businesses which engage in sound business practices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The Courts may then issue an injunction order against the recalcitrant retailer, and we will have the means to take this injunction and investigation action much quicker.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As part of the injunction order, the errant retailer may be required to publicise its injunction status, such as putting up notices within the shop premises and notifying potential customers of the injunction order, prior to them making a purchase, and thereby, stopping other tourists from falling prey.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This raises consumers' awareness and then the consumers, be they tourists or locals, can decide if they still want to purchase from this particular errant retailer.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The individuals who are involved in engaging in unfair practices may also have injunction orders issued against them and may be required to similarly publicise their injunction status.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This would prevent them from side-stepping the injunction orders.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: SPRING Singapore will also work with CASE to publicise the injunction orders issued by the Courts on errant retailers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Taken together, these measures will stop errant retailers from persisting in unfair practices and raise consumers' awareness of such retailers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Should errant retailers not comply with the Court orders, the administering agency has the power to take enforcement action.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The amendments send a strong deterrent signal to the small number of businesses which engage in unfair practices, for which they show a lack of respect for the law.
